evidence: The task reads as authored for HireOps rather than adapted by renaming. (1) Voice and product specifics: instruction.md:1-9 is a first-person recruiting-team ask ('the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day', 'when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who', 'Candidates sign in too ... described in the wording we use for candidates'); hireops_rules.md defines HireOps-only mechanics: roles Recruiter / Hiring manager / Observer / Candidate (1. table), interview places 1-50 per job (2, 3 'Interview places'), manager limited to Interview/Offer/Hired on own jobs (3 'Who may move what'), rejected-from-stage reopen rule, manual in-stage order shared by everyone, per-person undo invalidated by any later card change but not by notes (3 'Undo'), per-person unread and candidate/staff 'seen' semantics with observer exclusion (6), per-conversation drafts surviving session end with other-user isolation (6 'Drafts'), and a candidate wording table (7). Seed is HireOps-specific (10 users, 3 jobs, 16 applications, 127 messages incl. the 120-message Noor Haddad conversation per app_context.md:29-30, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size 30). (2) Criteria are product-authored: 44 functional rows all prefixed hro_ and tied to HireOps entities and seed facts (e.g. hro_restart names the seeded Platform Engineer order 'Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi; Screen: Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz'; hro_thread_access names Rafael/Mei/Bill/Ingrid/Noor), polish rows target HireOps live-update/draft/scroll-place behaviours (hro_pol_live_thread, hro_pol_earlier_place, hro_pol_session_resume), and the visual rows were rewritten from the template (template 'visual_typography ... Assess typography on the key screens' vs task 'hro_vis_type ... Judge desktop typography on the board, conversations and activity'; hro_vis_color mentions 'stage markers and the rejected stage'). A grep of the whole frozen task for every sibling product name (pellmoor, threadline, torquebay, bazaar, docketlight, boardloom, colderwater, ridgeline, gridforge, patchpad, coursemark, drawbill, oriel, medledger, orbital, expenseflow, utilibill) and for CHANGE_ME/TODO/FIXME returned nothing, so no copied prompt names another product. (3) Sibling comparison: the closest sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (same recruiting domain). Shared concepts are generic to hiring pipelines - one-step stage moves, a capacity limit and an all-or-none multi-card action. The flows and criteria differ materially: Pellmoor centres on interview panels with 1-5 scores, assessment versioning, offer-reserved vacancy openings, a d3 funnel from stage history and batch offers with a review/preview step, durable actor-scoped receipts and idempotent replay (hiring-rules.md:7-120; its functional prompt counts: panel 9, receipt 11, batch 11, funnel 3, and 0 undo/unread/draft/conversation/seen). HireOps has no panels, scores, funnel, receipts or offer-capacity, and instead grades interview-place capacity, shared manual ordering, undo (35 mentions), recruiter-candidate conversations (22), unread (7), seen (7), drafts, live updates that preserve focus/scroll/open card, and a candidate portal with data-leak refusals. Its rule wording also differs (Pellmoor: 'Only the hiring manager moves candidates'; HireOps: recruiters move anything, managers only late stages of their own jobs). threadline-chat shares chat mechanics (unread, load older without losing place) but is a channel/thread/reaction/webhook team chat without a pipeline or external-candidate party; torquebay is a repair-shop desk. None is the same flow set with renamed entities. (4) Domain plan: task.toml:5-15 declares name turing/hireops-recruiting-operations, arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations' (Pellmoor's slice is 'full-stack-typescript-d3-esbuild-express-sqlite-pipeline'), provenance 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task as a recruiting workspace, with an authored reference implementation and browser rubric', consistent with NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:203 (reuse infrastructure, author distinct domain behaviour). Counterexample probes: a nouns-swapped Pellmoor-style app (panels, scores, batch offers, funnel) would score near zero on the hro_ undo, conversation, unread, seen, drafts, candidate_view/private and live-update rows, so the rubric does not reward a sibling clone; conversely a conforming HireOps implementation is not penalised for lacking any sibling feature, because no criterion grades panels, receipts, funnels, reactions, webhooks or channels. Residual observation (not a defect): HireOps and Pellmoor both sit in recruiting; a portfolio owner may still want to note that two recruiting tasks exist, but the workspace holds no written suite domain plan that forbids it, and the assigned provenance says HireOps was supplied. This row is a source-level judgement; it needs no runtime measurement, and none was used or claimed.
